svg.font-family: Inter, 'Space Grotesk', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Dijkstra, A* and CCH find the same shortest route from Roma to Palermo
svg.desc: Three maps of the same Italian road network, 121 cities and 212 roads. Each lights up the cities a search has to look at before it knows the fastest route from Roma to Palermo, 11 h 21 min. Dijkstra settles 119 cities, spreading out in every direction from Roma. A* settles 54, leaning toward Palermo. A Customizable Contraction Hierarchy scans 23: the cities above Roma and above Palermo in its elimination tree, up to where the two climbs meet. All three return the same route, down Calabria and across the Strait of Messina.
svg.text: grows a circle around the start
climbs a hierarchy from both ends
Roma to Palermo, 11 h 21 min: same route, very different work
One dot per city the search has to look at, one city per tick in all three panels.
ArcadeDB Italy sample: 121 cities, 212 roads. Fastest route by travel time; A* estimates the time left from the straight line at 90 km/h.
CCH counts the cities on both elimination-tree climbs. Its hierarchy is built once, ahead of the queries, and kept up to date as the weights change.
